the usual weekend

You wanted to build an idea. Then you spent it on plumbing.

  • Pick and provision a database, then model your data twice
  • Wire up accounts, sessions and password resets
  • Add uploads, quotas and a place to put the files
  • Hide API keys behind a service you now have to host
  • Write migrations, deploy pipelines and monitoring before anyone sees the idea
with localme

Write the page. Call the API. Share the link.

  • Create a project — the URL, database and roles exist immediately
  • Drop in index.html and start fetching real data
  • Sign visitors in with the accounts the platform already manages
  • Keep keys encrypted and reach providers through a proxy route
  • Add a custom domain when it matters, not before

features

Twelve services you never have to build.

Each one is a documented HTTP API with session, API-key and role enforcement, rate limits and a matching console surface for configuration.

Data & files

Store the things your app creates and serve them back fast.

  • Document database/api/db/*

    A JSON store with a Mongo-style query DSL. Tables appear on first insert — no migrations, no schema.

  • File storage/api/storage/*

    Upload and stream any asset inside a hard quota that is checked before a single byte is written.

  • Shared asset library/library/*

    Keep one stylesheet or script for every project you own and reference it at /library/theme.css.

People & access

Know who is on the page and what they are allowed to do.

  • Visitor accounts/auth/*

    Signup, login, lockouts and a math CAPTCHA, hashed with scrypt-class cryptography. Bring your own login page or use ours.

  • Roles & permissionsrbac

    Owner, Admin, Member and Guest ship with each project, with 15 granular permissions and your own custom roles.

  • Encrypted secretssecrets

    AES-256-GCM at rest. Keys never reach a browser — call third parties through the proxy instead.

Ship & operate

Everything that turns a folder of files into a product.

  • Routing engineroutes

    Point any path at an HTML file and optionally require a login or a minimum role.

  • Reverse proxyproxy

    Forward requests to Stripe, OpenAI or your own API with {{SECRET}} header injection server-side.

  • Cron & webhooksautomation

    Five scheduled jobs per project plus nine signed webhook events with a full delivery log.

Trust & insight

The unglamorous parts that decide whether you can sleep.

  • Custom domainsdomains

    Prove ownership with a DNS TXT record; the platform handles certificates and routing.

  • Usage & limitslimits

    Storage, visits and rate limits are visible before they bite, with clear 402 and 429 responses.

  • Backups & auditaudit

    Export a project as an archive, restore it, and review every administrative action in the log.

how it works

From idea to a live URL in three steps.

No containers, no build pipeline, no database to provision. The platform runs one deployment and gives every project its own path, storage, data and credentials.

  1. 01
    Name a projectPOST /api/projects

    You get a live URL, a seeded welcome page, a PWA manifest, default roles, routes and cron configuration.

  2. 02
    Write frontend filesindex.html · style.css · app.js

    Edit HTML, CSS and JavaScript in the browser or upload them. Nothing is compiled and no server code is ever executed.

  3. 03
    Call the platformfetch('/api/db/find')

    Database, storage, accounts, proxied APIs and secrets are already there. Route it, gate it, share the link.

your project
served at /you/app/
/my-project/
├── index.html          ← routed at /
├── 404.html            ← your error page
├── login.html          ← optional custom login
├── manifest.json       ← PWA manifest (seeded)
├── sw.js               ← service worker (seeded)
└── static/
    ├── style.css       ← cached for a day
    └── app.js

# Reference one stylesheet from every project
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/library/theme.css">

# Talk to the platform from any page
const { data } = await fetch('/api/db/find', {
  method: 'POST',
  credentials: 'include',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ table: 'todos', filter: { done: false } })
}).then((r) => r.json());

use cases

Who ships on LocalMe

If your product is a great interface plus stored data, it fits. If it needs long-running server jobs or background workers, it does not — and we will tell you that up front.

Indie hackers

Validate an idea this weekend. Waitlists, feedback boards and paid micro-tools without standing up a backend repo.

AI-assisted builders

Point your coding agent at the API reference. Every endpoint is documented, so generated frontends work on the first run.

Students & courses

Teach real full-stack ideas without provisioning databases. Accounts, data and files are one fetch call away.

Agencies & freelancers

Ship small client sites with a form inbox, a CMS table and a password-protected preview area. Same account for all of them.

Internal tools

Ops dashboards, checklists and trackers that live behind a login and cost nothing to keep running.

Hobby projects

Give your game, club or community site a real scoreboard, guestbook or poll that survives a refresh.
